turns.message: Before we go anywhere — what have you got in front of you? An album, a box of prints, some paperwork, someone on the phone — or nothing at all, which is fine too.
A shoebox is a good start. Pull out one you can't place at all, and tell me what's in the frame — and what's near it: the envelope, the back, the sleeve it came in.

The tree is up and the car in the driveway is the Country Squire you had between '86 and '88 — so that one sits inside that window rather than on any single day. A photograph gives a window, not a date, and I'd rather keep the window honest.
The report card is printed 12 June 1984 — you'd remembered it as the spring. I'll keep both; the paper and the memory are two different kinds of witness, and the paper is the one with a date on it.
Your mom says you moved in in '84 — I've put that down as hers, in her words. That's second-hand by nature, so I'm holding it as approximate rather than settled.
Wildwood Elementary, 1220 Wildwood Avenue in Yucaipa — the street is the piece that matters, because an address gives us the district, and a district keeps records with exact years in them.
Then that one's at your sister's, and it can stay there. What have you got to hand instead?
Good hour. We put the Yucaipa years on the map and dated the report card to the day; your mom would know the rest of the addresses, and that list is on her page whenever you want it.
